posts.text:
Your AI tools didn't fail you.

They just scaled the mess you already had.

Every week I talk to a B2B founder who did everything right on paper.

Bought the ABM platform.
Hired the AI SDR.
Wired up the automation.

And pipeline got worse.

Here's the part nobody likes hearing:

AI doesn't fix bad data. It moves it faster.
Automation doesn't fix unclear ownership. It just multiplies the confusion.
ABM doesn't fix a GTM you're running as random campaigns. It spends more money on the same chaos.

The tool was never the bottleneck. The foundation under it was.

Most teams in 2026 aren't really debating AI strategy. They're quietly asking a smaller, scarier question: do we even trust our own CRM data?

If the answer is no, every new tool you bolt on makes it worse.

So before the next platform demo, fix the boring layer:

Data every team actually trusts.
Clear ownership across marketing, sales, and success.
A GTM that works like a system, not a string of launches.

Do that, and the same tools that embarrassed you last quarter start to compound.

Foundation first. Then automation.

What's the most expensive tool you've seen underdeliver because the foundation wasn't ready?

A client's SDR was sending hundreds of LinkedIn messages a month. Reply rate barely moved.

The problem wasn't volume. It was the absence of signal.

No one knew which message worked, on which channel, for which target. So they kept scaling the same broken approach.

We rebuilt the system on LaGrowthMachine. Reply rate landed around 20%.

Here's the architecture:

1️⃣ A/B Testing layer
 Every campaign runs message variants against each other before scaling. We don't guess which hook works, we test it on a small batch first, then push budget behind the winner.

2️⃣ isActive? filter on LinkedIn
 LGM checks whether a profile is actually active before a message goes out. Sounds small. It's the difference between burning outreach quota on ghost accounts and spending it on people who'll actually see the message.

3️⃣ Real Chat Mode
 Messages route through a setup that reads like an actual conversation, not a sequence. This is what gets replies instead of silence or "unsubscribe."

4️⃣ Deal tracking by campaign
 We tied every campaign to revenue outcomes, not just reply counts. A campaign with high replies and zero deals isn't a win. This layer is what tells you which campaign to kill and which to double down on.

What I'd do differently: build the deal-tracking layer first next time, not last. Knowing which campaign drives revenue should shape the A/B tests from day one, not just grade them after.

If your agency's moat is "we connect SaaS tools to each other"... it's time to move up the stack.

How GTM-ready is your company for AI?

Answer these 5 questions honestly:

Data Quality Score Your CRM has clean, complete records without duplicates A) Yes, 90%+ clean B) Mostly, but some gaps C) Honestly? It's a mess

Lead Scoring Sophistication How do you currently identify hot vs cold leads? A) AI-powered predictive model B) Manual scoring by account age + activity C) Whoever the rep thinks is worth calling

GTM Channel Alignment Sales, marketing, and RevOps are aligned on process A) Complete alignment, same metrics B) Mostly aligned but some friction C) Completely siloed

Automation Maturity What percentage of your GTM workflows are automated? A) 60%+ (routing, nurture, scoring) B) 20-40% (some automation, mostly manual) C) <10% (mostly manual)

AI Adoption Are you using AI for GTM decisions? A) Yes, actively (lead scoring, intent, routing) B) Experimenting, not fully leveraging C) Haven't started

Scoring:
↳ Mostly A's: You're ahead. Let's optimize.
↳ Mix of A's & B's: You've got foundations. AI can unlock 3-5x here.
↳ Mix of B's & C's: You have significant GTM gaps. AI won't fix these alone—need strategy first.
↳ Mostly C's: Your competitors are running circles around you with AI. This is the quarter to act.

If you scored B's or C's in data quality, lead scoring, or automation—that's where the biggest GTM improvements live.

The companies hitting +50% GTM growth are solving these exactly in this order:

↳ Data cleanup
↳ AI-powered lead scoring
↳ Intent-based routing
↳ Multichannel automation

Last quarter, I worked with a B2B SaaS company doing 2.5M ARR.

Their GTM was chaos:

↳ Sales blaming marketing for bad leads 
↳ Marketing blaming sales for not following up 
↳ RevOps caught in the middle with a broken forecasting model 
↳ Sales cycle averaging 65 days (should be 30-40)

They needed an AI-GTM overhaul.

Here's exactly what we did:

Before (Month 1):
Lead scoring: Manual (guesswork)
Lead routing: Random to whoever was available
Forecasting: Excel model, 50% accuracy
Cadence: One-size-fits-all email/call sequence

Result: 12% monthly sales growth, declining

Implementation (Months 2-3):

Step 1: Deploy predictive lead scoring 

↳ Built AI model on their best-fit customers 
↳ Trained it to spot buying signals (job changes, website behavior, funding announcements) 
↳ Result: Top 20% of leads scored as "hot" were 3.2x more likely to convert

Step 2: Create intent-based routing 

↳ Hot leads → AE immediately (don't wait) 
↳ Warm leads → SDR nurture sequence (3-week warm-up) 
↳ Cold leads → Marketing automation (keep warm, revisit quarterly)

Step 3: Automate GTM workflows 

↳ LinkedIn + Email sequences triggered by buying signals 
↳ Used La Growth Machine for multichannel automation 
↳ Timing: LinkedIn message 2 hours after email open, phone call 24 hours after LinkedIn reply 
↳ Why: Meeting them on their preferred channel

After (Month 4):

Sales cycle: 32 days (was 65)
Close rate: 23% (was 14%)
Forecast accuracy: 78% (was 50%)
Sales cycle length dropped by 49%
Win rate on hot leads: 41% vs 9% on cold leads
Monthly growth: 34% (was 12%)

Key metrics: 

↳ +60% revenue impact in 90 days 
↳ Sales team gained 8 hours/week back 
↳ RevOps had predictable data for the first time

The real win? They stopped treating all prospects the same. Hot leads with buying signals got treated like hot leads. Cold prospects got evergreen nurture.

Result: Higher conversion, lower wasted effort, predictable GTM.

The lesson: AI-GTM isn't about more touches. It's about smarter touches to the right people at the right time.

If your GTM feels scattered and your sales cycle is too long, we can run the same playbook for you: https://lnkd.in/gyjBPA44
